The gain weight first thing is bullshit. What will work better is what the fitness world refers to as bulking, you train hard while eating at a slight surplus (men about a lb a week or 500 calories per day). Start by picking a structured program for strength training, I personally liked Stronglifts 5x5 and Starting Strength. Both of those programs are easily searchable on google for templates and how to's. Eat as needed or to maintenance for the first while until you start to stall (not be able to do the weight for the required sets or reps). Once you stall you start eating more to grow your muscles bigger so you can do the program. This avoids unnecessary fat gain while you are starting out. Half of weight lifting is neural adaptation. And I know it will feel silly to start with an empty bar but it actually does work because it allows you to learn form early. Also squat to depth from the beginning, break parallel!

As for what to eat try eating more calorie dense foods instead of eating more (dark meat instead of light, avocados, peanut butter, pork or beef instead of fish or chicken, while milk instead of skim). Small changes make a big difference. Also into a protein shake you can make additions like peanut butter or milk instead of water. If you just aren't a fan of eating then you can use a weight gainer protein shake (supplement stores have it).

Feel free to ask away if you have more questions. :)
